title: Vulkan from Zero
description: An interactive, visual Vulkan course for graphics people: every object, frame and barrier you can see and step through, with Rust (ash) and C++ (Vulkan-Hpp) code.

modules.title: Foundations
modules.summary: What a GPU is, how a program gets work onto it, why Vulkan is explicit, and the map of every Vulkan object.

lessons.title: What a GPU is
lessons.summary: Thousands of small cores, its own memory, and why it is fast at pixels and slow at decisions.

lessons.title: How a program talks to the GPU
lessons.summary: Application, driver, command buffers and queues: the path every draw call takes.

lessons.title: Why Vulkan exists
lessons.summary: OpenGL's hidden state machine versus Vulkan's explicit objects, and what you pay and get for it.

lessons.title: The map of Vulkan objects
lessons.summary: Every object of a Vulkan program on one map: who creates whom, and in what order.

modules.title: Instance
modules.summary: Install the tools, create the first Vulkan object and turn on the validation layers that will catch our mistakes.

lessons.title: Toolchain: SDK, Rust and C++ projects
lessons.summary: Vulkan SDK, vulkaninfo, vkconfig, and the two example projects: Rust with ash, C++ with Vulkan-Hpp.

lessons.title: The loader and VkInstance
lessons.summary: How the Vulkan loader finds drivers, and what an instance, layers and extensions are.

lessons.title: Validation layers and the debug messenger
lessons.summary: Layers that check every call against the spec, and how their messages reach our code.

modules.title: Devices and queues
modules.summary: Pick a GPU, learn what it can do, find its engines (queue families) and open a logical device with queues.

lessons.title: Physical devices: properties, features, limits
lessons.summary: Enumerating GPUs and reading what each one is and can do.

lessons.title: Queue families: the GPU's engines
lessons.summary: Graphics, compute, transfer: how queue families relate to the hardware engines inside the GPU.

lessons.title: Logical device and queues
lessons.summary: Opening a VkDevice with the features and queues we chose, and getting VkQueue handles.

modules.title: Presentation
modules.summary: Open a window, connect Vulkan to it through a surface, and build the swapchain: the ring of images the screen shows in turn.

lessons.title: A window and its surface
lessons.summary: Vulkan knows no windows: the WSI extensions, VkSurfaceKHR, and asking the GPU what it can show in our window.

lessons.title: The swapchain and present modes
lessons.summary: A ring of images owned by the presentation engine: format, present mode, size and image count.

lessons.title: Images and image views
lessons.summary: What a VkImage is, and why rendering and shaders look at images through VkImageView.

modules.title: The graphics pipeline
modules.summary: Shaders in Slang compiled to SPIR-V, the stages of the graphics pipeline, its layout, and rendering without render passes.

lessons.title: Shaders, Slang and SPIR-V
lessons.summary: From shader source to SPIR-V to a VkShaderModule: Vulkan's one binary shader format and how our triangle shader gets there.

lessons.title: The graphics pipeline object
lessons.summary: Every stage from vertex input to color blending baked into one VkPipeline, and the state left dynamic.

lessons.title: The pipeline layout
lessons.summary: The declaration of every resource a pipeline's shaders may read: descriptor set layouts and push constant ranges.

lessons.title: Dynamic rendering
lessons.summary: Rendering into image views named at record time: attachments, load and store operations, and what replaced VkRenderPass.

modules.title: Commands and the first triangle
modules.summary: Record commands into a command buffer, submit it to a queue, and put the first triangle on the screen.

lessons.title: Command pools and command buffers
lessons.summary: Where command buffers come from, what recording means, and how a submission reaches the queue.

lessons.title: The first triangle
lessons.summary: One frame end to end: wait, acquire, record, submit, present, with a fence, semaphores and two layout transitions.

labs.title: Warp divergence
labs.summary: 32 lanes, one instruction stream: write a condition and watch the warp run both branches with lanes switched off.

labs.title: Where the data lives
labs.summary: VRAM, system RAM and the PCIe bus between them, with the real bandwidths of the course GPU: what a frame costs if a buffer crosses the bus.

labs.title: The path of a command
labs.summary: CPU records, submits, moves on; the GPU runs the work later. A CPU/GPU timeline you can scrub.

labs.title: OpenGL state vs Vulkan pipelines
labs.summary: Change state in a GL-style driver and see when it has to rebuild a shader behind your back; do the same with prebuilt Vulkan pipelines.

labs.title: Through the loader
labs.summary: Pick a Vulkan call and the enabled layers, then follow it from the trampoline through the layers to the terminator and the drivers.

labs.title: Debug messenger filters
labs.summary: Severity and type masks applied to a real validation log: which messages reach your callback.

labs.title: Pick a GPU
labs.summary: The real properties, features and limits of the course GPU, and the picking rule of step 03 that you can change.

labs.title: Queue planner
labs.summary: The real queue families of the course GPU: choose graphics, async compute and transfer queues and see what you get.

labs.title: Build the object tree
labs.summary: Create and destroy Vulkan objects in any order; the simulator answers with the real validation rules.

labs.title: Queues, semaphores and fences
labs.summary: Submit batches to several queues with wait and signal semaphores and a fence: see what overlaps, what waits and where a race appears.

labs.title: The graphics pipeline
labs.summary: Walk the stages from vertex input to color output, and see which state is baked into a pipeline and which is dynamic in Vulkan 1.4.

labs.title: Buffers and memory
labs.summary: From buffer usage to memory requirements to a memory type of the real course GPU, and a staging upload or a direct write through the BAR window.
